headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Claude Code can write shared files while gpt-researcher reads and publishes research outputs without documented verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code can write repo files and use MCP, while gpt-researcher reads local documents and uses MCP/APIs. That creates a plausible shared-file or shared-MCP injection path where attacker-controlled content from one agent can be treated as instructions by the other. The interaction is documented only at profile level, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or MCP server
IF gpt-researcher ingests files written by Claude Code as instructions
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable shared MCP servers for the pair
Require a human review step before either agent consumes the other's files
Prefix inter-agent handoffs with machine-readable provenance markers
requires-engineering: add sandboxed provenance filtering between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents read local files and have broad network egress, so sensitive repo or document contents can flow from one agent into the other's outputs or API calls. Claude Code explicitly touches source code, git history, and secrets in environment; gpt-researcher touches local documents and research reports. The shared workspace plus outbound APIs makes leakage plausible in default setups.
conditions: IF either agent is given secrets, private source code, or confidential documents
IF both agents operate in the same directory or on the same mounted workspace
mitigations: Use separate directories and separate credentials
Remove secrets from the shared workspace before running either agent
Turn off network egress for the agent handling sensitive files
Review outbound API destinations for both agents
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files and spawn subprocesses, and Claude Code also modifies git state. Their concurrency models only mention filesystem/git sharing for Claude Code and no locking for gpt-researcher, so simultaneous edits to the same repo can corrupt state or overwrite work. Because the default overlap includes mutable filesystem and git resources, this is high.
conditions: IF both agents are run against the same git repository
IF either agent commits or rewrites files while the other is active
mitigations: Run only one agent per repository at a time
Use separate branches for each agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Review git diffs before merge
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transactional workspace coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher produces research reports, citations, and publisher outputs, while Claude Code can act on files and git state. If Claude Code consumes gpt-researcher output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into code changes or published artifacts. No verification or provenance controls are documented in either profile, so the unsafe default is high.
conditions: IF Claude Code uses gpt-researcher reports as direct instructions
IF gpt-researcher output is not independently checked before code or publication actions
mitigations: Require a human verification step before acting on research outputs
Cross-check claims against primary sources
Mark gpt-researcher output as untrusted input in prompts
Limit Claude Code to read-only review until verification passes
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware gating between research and action agents

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code explicitly handles git credentials and source code, while gpt-researcher handles local documents, citations, and multiple external APIs. If regulated or personal data is placed into the shared workflow, the pair can create retention, residency, or third-party disclosure mismatches. The profiles do not document aligned compliance controls, so the risk is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated personal data, customer data, or secrets are processed by both agents
IF the deployment requires retention or residency controls that differ across the agents' APIs
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the shared workspace
Use separate API keys and retention settings
Confirm data-processing terms for each external API
Delete intermediate reports after review
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies across the pair
